label: Information Systems
text: People, processes and data — and how they turn input into information.

label: Information Systems
text: An information system is implemented for automating processes, reducing human errors and improving efficiency.

label: Information Systems
text: Computer engineer: design, build and integrate the hardware, software and network.

label: Information Systems
text: Systems analyst: design a system to fulfil the business needs and the requirements provided by end users. Analyse the time, cost and feasibility of building the system.

label: Information Systems
text: Programmer: develop the system according to the design given by systems analysts.

label: Number Systems
text: Binary, hexadecimal, signed integers, two's complement and character encoding.

label: Number Systems
text: People usually use a decimal system (also known as denary system) for counting. In contrast, digital devices use a binary system.

label: Number Systems
text: Binary numbers are used because each digit of a binary number can represent one bit (21) of digital data.

label: Number Systems
text: A decimal number is a number in base 10, while a binary number is a number in base 2.

label: Number Systems
text: A hexadecimal number is a number in base 16. It's commonly used because each digit can represent 4 bits (24) of digital data.

label: Number Systems
text: Each binary digit represents 1 bit; each hex digit represents 4 bits.

label: Number Systems
text: One bit of data is transferred every second

label: Number Systems
text: Hexadecimal digits use 0–9 and A–F (A = 10, B = 11, C = 12, D = 13, E = 14, F = 15).

label: Number Systems
text: Unsigned integers only include positive integers and zero.

label: Number Systems
text: An unsigned integer represented in N-bits ranges from 0 to 2N − 1. For example, if we allocate 3 bits to store an unsigned integer, it can be as small as 0 (000) and as large as 23 − 1 = 7 (111).

label: Number Systems
text: Signed integers include positive integers, negative integers and zero.

label: Number Systems
text: A signed integer represented in N-bits usually ranges from −2N−1 to 2N−1 − 1. For example, if we allocate 3 bits to store a signed integer, it can be as small as −23−1 = −4 and as large as 23−1 − 1 = 3.

label: Number Systems
text: e.g. To represent 2710 in 6 bits, we simply convert 2710 into a 6-digit binary number, which is 011011, instead of 11011.

label: Number Systems
text: Drawback: two representations of zero exist — positive zero (+0) and negative zero (−0).

label: Number Systems
text: Two's complement: a method for representation of signed integers in bit pattern.

label: Number Systems
text: For a two's complement representation: if the first bit is 0, it represents a non-negative number; if the first bit is 1, it represents a negative number.

label: Number Systems
text: The two's complement of an integer X is the two's complement representation of −X. For example, the two's complement of 310 is 101, which is also the two's complement representation of −310.

label: Number Systems
text: English: American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) is one of the commonly used character encoding systems. ASCII usually uses 7 bits to represent a character (letters, numbers, symbols). Sometimes, ASCII is extended to 8 bits (1 byte) because of one of the following reasons:

label: Number Systems
text: It can represent more characters by using the extra bit

label: Number Systems
text: It can use the extra bit as a parity bit

label: Number Systems
text: Some systems process data in a byte

label: Number Systems
text: Traditional Chinese is often encoded by Big-5 code

label: Number Systems
text: Simplified Chinese is often encoded by Guobiao (GB) code

label: Number Systems
text: Both encoding systems use 2 bytes (16 bits) to store a character and contain over 10000 characters, including English letters, digits and symbols.

label: Number Systems
text: Both encoding systems are not interchangeable. If a text file or a website is encoded by Big-5 code, but is decoded by Guobiao code, instead of being translated to simplified Chinese, the text will be displayed as garbled text.

label: Number Systems
text: If multiple languages are expected in a text file or a website, a character encoding system named Unicode will be used.

label: Number Systems
text: Unicode can be extended to represent 1000000 characters.

label: Digitalisation
text: Analog vs digital data, sampling, quantisation and file size.

label: Digitalisation
text: There are different ways to represent a piece of data:

label: Digitalisation
text: Analog data (模擬資料) is represented in a physical way with continuous values, such as sound waves, written text and drawings.

label: Digitalisation
text: Digital data (數碼資料) is represented in discrete symbols (like "0" and "1"), such as text documents, digital photos and audio files. It is usually stored and used in devices like computers and smartphones.

label: Digitalisation
text: Analog data storage examples: photographic films, cassette tape

label: Digitalisation
text: Digital data storage: memory cards in digital cameras, optical discs

label: Digitalisation
text: Digitalisation is the conversion of analog data to digital data. We can break down digitalisation into two parts: discretisation and quantisation.

label: Digitalisation
text: Take analog signal as an example. An analog signal can take on uncountable set of continuous values. Its quantity varies from time to time.

label: Digitalisation
text: To convert an analog signal into a digital signal, the value of the signal should be sampled at a regular time interval. The length of this time interval determines the sampling rate. This process is called discretisation.

label: Digitalisation
text: After discretisation, sampled values are rounded to a fixed set of discrete values, such as integers.

label: Digitalisation
text: The analog signal is stored as a sequence of integers. This sequence is digital data, which is usually represented by binary numbers in digital storage. This process is called quantisation.

label: Digitalisation
text: A higher sampling rate means more samples are taken in a given period of time. The resulting data is thus closer to the original waveform and has less data loss during digitalisation.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Image types, attributes, compression and file formats for multimedia.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: There are two types of images:

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Bitmap images are stored as a series of little squares called pixels. Vector images are stored as mathematical formulae, which connect points to draw lines, curves, circles, polygons, etc.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: • Real life digital photos are usually bitmap images • It can be edited by common image editing software like Microsoft Paint

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: • Its file size tends to be smaller • It does not have rough edges and will not become blurry when scaled up or down • Usually used for logos or animations

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: An image file has four important attributes: resolution, colour depth, aspect ratio and transparency.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Colour depth is the number of bits used to represent the colour of a pixel. The higher the colour depth an image has, the more colours it can include.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Resolution is the total number of pixels in an image. It is usually represented as "number of pixels per row × number of pixels per column", i.e. "width × height".

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: The aspect ratio is the ratio of an image's width to its height. Common ratios include 4:3 and 16:9. When an image is placed into a container of a different aspect ratio, you can either leave blank spaces (letterboxing) or crop the image.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Transparency means that whether an image can have transparent areas or not.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Relatively large file size. Usually supports 24-bit colour depth.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Relatively small file size. Usually supports 24-bit colour depth.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Lossless compression is supported. Compressed SVG is called SVGZ.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Image quality / size / compression ratio (from previous notes)

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Lossless compression means no data is lost after compression. The original file can be retrieved completely once decompressed.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Text string, SSSSSSMON3D3D3D3D3DAAAABBBAAAABBBAAA, contains 40 characters. To represent this string using fewer characters, we may follow the steps below:

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Count the number of the same repeating patterns and add that number before the patterns 6SSSSSS1MON53D3D3D3D4AAAA3BBB3AAA3BBB3AAA3BBB2AA

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: If that pattern contains backslash, add a backslash before every backslash.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: If that pattern contains numbers, enclose it with backslashes to avoid confusion. 6SSSSSS1MON5\3D3D3D3D3D\4AAA\3BBB3AAA3BBB3AAA3BBB2AA

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Delete all but one repeating pattern 6S1MON5\3D\4A3B3A3B3A2A

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Lossy compression means some data is lost after compression.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: (Best audio quality) (Largest file size) Uncompressed, lossless compression, lossy compression (Smallest file size) (Worst audio quality)

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Note that uncompressed audio and lossless compressed audio have the same level of audio quality.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: An audio file has three important attributes: bit depth, sampling rate and the number of channels.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Bit depth is the number of bits used to represent an audio sample. The higher the bit depth an audio has, the more sound levels it can represent and the better quality it has.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Sampling rate is the number of audio samples taken per second. The higher the sampling rate an audio has, the more samples are captured in a period of time. This means the audio is closer to the original sound wave and hence has better quality.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Number of channels: sometimes, an audio file has more than one channel.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: A video is a sequence of images shown within a certain duration and potentially one or more audio tracks. A video file has four important attributes: colour depth, resolution, frame rate and duration.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Frame rate (fps) is the number of frames shown per second.

label: Multimedia & Compression

label: Multimedia & Compression

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Multimedia (text, image, video, audio) can be stored in various file formats and have different attributes. The file format and the metadata of a file are usually stored in its file header.

label: Multimedia & Compression
text: Different file formats are supported by different software and operating systems. Some file formats involve compression and suffer from data loss while some do not.
